verdict.text: All three round 1 findings are fixed, and the fixes broke nothing.
The README names both things APM cannot install.
The .gitignore comment explains the slop-scan-for-docs whitelist line.
The recipe test now pins the copied rule set to the 7.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: "stamp green: f4836b6b0b24cf8b6ad5166e65f1cdcca2aae9188218ac006820325d9437880f", with gates pre_commit and cli_tests and rows r1 to r8 passing.
README.md lines 96 to 104: the paragraph now says APM cannot install two things, then names slop-scan-for-docs (committed in `.claude/rules/`) and caveman (added by hand).
That matches the .gitignore whitelist and apm.yml.
r7's README tests still pass on it.
.gitignore lines 22 to 25: the comment now covers slop-scan-for-docs, and the whitelist lines are unchanged.

cli/tests/test_agent_tooling.py: `test_opencode_rules_come_from_both_install_recipes` extracts every `.claude/rules/NAME.md` from each recipe and asserts the set equals RULES (the 6 APM rules plus slop-scan-for-docs).
Both justfile cp lines name exactly those 7.
A glob would also fail the set check because `*` matches the name pattern, and the explicit glob assertion stays.
The set equality closes the "rule outside the 7" gap.
The byte comparison is still conditional, but its docstring now names r8 as the proof on a clean checkout, which is the reason I asked for.
